R1875.summary: Sebastiano Foscarini, Venetian ambassador in Spain, to the Doge and Senate: the court has moved to the Escorial; the broken-off peace talks between London and Versailles feed conjecture in Madrid, some holding that Spain can no longer look on while France is beaten in America, others that Charles III will stay neutral; the first foresee a union with 'another court' (NOTES.md takes this to be the Third Family Compact with France, signed 15 August 1761 and still secret; the text does not name it).
R1875.en:
Most Serene Prince.

No. 178. Sole copy.

As I had the honour of reporting to Your Excellencies, on Wednesday His Majesty and the whole Royal family moved to
this residence. The short distance to where I too have come, prompted by my most respectful desire to show Your
Serenity in every best way the true commitment of my good will, and moved by the troubled configuration of the
present times, which demand the greatest vigilance, as they would need an enlightened and active mind to ease the
way to knowledge of those dealings which, in every respect, may concern the wisdom of the Most Excellent Senate.
The broken-off negotiations between the Courts of London and Versailles are the source from which spring endless
conjectures and political systems.

system: Numerical cipher of Italian (alphabet plus syllabary per crittologia.eu on Foscarini's ciphers); groups separated by points.
